sermon.title: Other Things as Well
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 1:3-4 that believers are called to be partakers of the divine nature. He traces the first promise in Genesis 3:15, the woman’s seed bruising Satan’s head, and says Jesus and His church have rendered Satan powerless. He then uses the parable of the wheat and the tares in Matthew 13 to explain why the good and bad seed grow together, and how behavior shows who are children of God and who are children of the devil.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: for the passage about tread on serpents and scorpions he says “Luke 10:17”; the words are in Luke 10:19, which is the passage shown. He also says “John 3:10” for “this is how we know who the children of God are,” which is 1 John 3:10, and the caption gave “Matthew 30 13330” where he means Matthew 13:30. His seed-company source is given in the captions as “Burpee and Gerber,” which was left as heard. The captions wrote “tears”; this was corrected to “tares.” “[Unclear]” marks two spots where the captions were not clear. He makes claims about botany (darnel), about the pre-tribulation rapture, about men and women, and about people he names as opponents; those are his words, not verified by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud he often uses King James wording.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)
chunks.short_answer: He says 2 Peter 1:3-4 gives “exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” “We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game.” He says Christians tend to look elsewhere, but being participators in God’s nature “needs to be a high priority in our life.”

In 2 Peter 1:3-4: “As Jesus the divine power has given us all things,” “whereby by these things are given us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” Okay, participators of the divine nature. We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game. We’re participants. Okay, now American Christians have a tendency to look for the second coming, a prosperity, purpose, positive confessions, focusing on the poor instead of the divine nature, or phenomenal--

Miracles and so forth. We have a tendency to look for gifts and all that, and a lot of groups focus on different areas, uh, some on soul-winning and so forth, but God very strongly puts in His Word that there are promises that we can be participators in the divine nature, God’s nature, and so that needs to be a high priority in our life. chunks.section_question: Why does Satan go after the weak and the stragglers? (Deuteronomy 25:18)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Deuteronomy 25:18, where Amalek attacked the rear of Israel, “the feeble ones, the weary ones, the weak ones that were behind.” He says we become weak when we do not feed on the Word, since “the Word of God is our food,” and “the stragglers are the ones that don’t nourish themselves.” It is imperative, he says, that newborn Christians “not stay weak, but grow quickly to the young man’s stage.”
chunks.text:
To get you to backslide, you see, and the only thing he can’t touch you, so he touches the direction you’re going, get you distracted. In this case the horse reared up and you fell off, and so forth. So this helps us understand “bruising the heel.” In Deuteronomy 25:18, remember Amalek? Amalek is the, the tribe of people that came while Israel was in the wilderness and attacked the rear part of Israel. Okay, “Remember Amalek, how he met you by the way and smote the rear most of you.” You see, the heel, the rear most. And what people make up the rear most? “All that were feeble behind--

You,” “and when you was--was faint and weary,” he came and smote the feeble ones, the weary ones, the weak ones that were behind. Now, how do we become weak? Well, you become weak in the natural if you don’t eat. Try not eating for 30 days and see how good you can travel. Try not eating for seven days and just see how good you can travel. You’re back there dragging your feet. Try not drinking for seven days and see how you travel. You’re going to be crawling. And see, the Word of God is our food, the Bible says, and when we don’t feed on the Word of God, we get what? Weak. The Holy Spirit is the water. The Word is the water too, but--and when we don’t get into His presence, we get weak and we drag behind.

Everybody’s four miles ahead and here we are, “Oh, I will bless the Lord at all times.” Oh yeah. Why? Because we haven’t fed ourselves, we haven’t taken care of ourselves. Another way you get weak is no exercise. You sit on the couch all day, your joints don’t move right, things get weak, the muscles don’t work right. And so we have to exercise the Bible, we have to feed on the Bible, and we got to drink. Could that be an amen? And the stragglers are the ones that don’t nourish themselves, and Satan comes and gets them, fights with them. Okay, he bruises the weak.

The young man stage not only keeps the Word, but the Word abides in him, the Scripture abides in him, and he overcomes the evil one and overcomes evil. So we need to grow to that stage so we’re not stragglers and Satan can come and bruise us and crush us. Are you with me? Did God keep His promise? These are questions I ask God: “God, did You back this up? Did You really do--

chunks.section_question: How much power does Satan really have?
chunks.short_answer: He says “the church out there has given way too much credit to Satan.” Even in Job’s story Satan “had to get permission from God to do it.” He says Satan can suggest and roar, but is “a lion that has no teeth and no claws,” and God’s promise is to “destroy sin and Satan, not destroy you.”
chunks.text:
Means nothing. See, we don’t pick up serpents, we don’t pick up scorpions, we step on Satan and his demonic powers with the weakest part of our body, our heel. Hallelujah. See, you say, “Well, that was to the apostles.” Well, God is no respecter of persons. He’s going to give that to the apostles, and He’s not going to give that to His church? Come on. You see, so it’s a very powerful thing, and see, the church needs to understand that Satan has been rendered powerless. The church out there has given way too much credit to Satan, way too much. Now, don’t get me wrong, even in the Old Testament, Satan, you know, he came and he took Job’s wealth, he took his health and killed his kids and so forth, but he had to get permission from God to do it. You see, everybody thinks Satan is just a loose goose out here doing what he want. He can’t do anything, and never could, without his Creator saying, “Okay,” and the Creator always has a what? Purpose in letting Satan do what he can--

Do. And in the New Testament it’s the same way. See, when Paul said, “We wanted to go to another city, but Satan hinders us,” okay, and, and if you really study and read it, it wasn’t really Satan, it was the people there hindering them going over there. chunks.section_question: How do we put Satan under our feet and share in God’s nature?
chunks.short_answer: He says “Jesus destroyed Satan through his death on the cross, he has no control over us. We ourselves put Satan under our feet, and now we can become a partaker, a participant, of the divine nature.” He lists God’s attributes, righteous, holy, wise, knowledgeable and good, that “we can have and shine like a light in this darkened world.”
chunks.text: Know what the good seed is and the bad seed. Now we know Jesus destroyed Satan through his death on the cross, he has no control over us. We ourselves put Satan under our feet, and now we can become a partaker, a participant, of the divine nature. God is righteous, God is holy, God is wise, God is knowledgeable, God is good, all these attributes of God we can have, and shine like a light in this darkened world and hopefully bring many tares to be converted to Christ. Amen.

faqs.question: What does he say American Christians tend to focus on instead of the divine nature?
faqs.answer: He says they “have a tendency to look for the second coming,” prosperity, purpose, positive confessions, miracles and gifts, and that groups focus on different areas such as soul-winning.

scriptures.text_nkjv: as His divine power has given to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by glory and virtue, by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

faqs.question: How does he say we should read the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says not just to read it through for the year: “you have to inquire of God and ask Him questions, and/or let the Holy Spirit ask you questions.”

faqs.question: Can the word in Genesis 3:15 be read as “it,” “he” or “she”?
faqs.answer: He says it is a third-person singular word that can be used as “it,” “he” or “she” depending on the sentence. With “he” it refers to Jesus, and with “she” he says it refers to the church.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I will put enmity Between you and the woman, And between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, And you shall bruise His heel.”

faqs.question: Why does he say the church is the “she”?
faqs.answer: He says the church, the bride of Christ, is “always referred to in the Bible as feminine,” so “she” the church shall bruise Satan’s head.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, A viper by the path, That bites the horse’s heels So that its rider shall fall backward.

faqs.question: How does he say believers keep from being weak?
faqs.answer: He says “we have to exercise the Bible, we have to feed on the Bible, and we got to drink.” Not exercising or feeding leaves us weak and dragging behind.

faqs.question: Does he say the devil is chasing every Christian?
faqs.answer: No. He says that when he grew up in church ministers tried to cast the devil out of the church, but “there’s no Bible for that. Satan is rendered powerless when we come to Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

faqs.question: Was it really Satan who hindered Paul?
faqs.answer: He says when Paul said Satan hindered them, “if you really study and read it, it wasn’t really Satan, it was the people there hindering them going over there.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but Satan hindered us.

faqs.question: If something bad happens, is God or Satan punishing me?
faqs.answer: He says we need to “get off this mentality” that a car wreck or lost job comes because of a little white lie or a bad attitude. “He’s not out to condemn you and destroy you.”

faqs.question: Why does he say the tares should not be pulled up?
faqs.answer: He says the tare’s root “entangles itself with the root of the wheat,” so pulling it up pulls up wheat too. “He don’t want you being rooted up before you have a chance to produce fruit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”

faqs.question: What does he mean by the “herding instinct” in young believers?
faqs.answer: He says young believers and young people “have the herding instinct”: whatever the other young people are doing, they want to do it, such as wearing certain clothes or hairstyles.

faqs.question: Can a tare be converted into wheat?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “a lot of these tares can be converted and change their nature and become wheat,” so pulling one out may remove “someone that can be converted.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”

faqs.question: Why does he say people dislike Christmas and Easter?
faqs.answer: He says they “don’t like Christmas because it refers to Christ” and don’t like Easter because it refers to His death and resurrection, so they bring in the Easter bunny to distract.

faqs.question: Does he say a baptismal certificate or the sinner’s prayer proves you are a child of God?
faqs.answer: He says no: “it’s got nothing to do with your baptismal certificate,” your time at the altar, saying the sinner’s prayer, or being raised a Baptist or a Catholic. “Anyone who doesn’t do what is right is not a child of God.”
